first.rationale: Both onboarding completion (-4% QoQ) and activation (-6% QoQ) are declining. Memory_31 and memory_86 directly address onboarding simplification and show durable lift in activation and completion rates. These are the highest-confidence levers for the current problem. Verifying these two memories ensures the foundational claims are sound before committing resources. Simplify_onboarding addresses both metrics simultaneously and aligns with established evidence. Promotional_pricing risks eroding margins and may only temporarily address competitor pressure; referral_incentive assumes healthy activation (which is currently down); enterprise_sales_assist doesn't address the activation decline affecting self-serve accounts. A standard_experiment allows reasonable signal detection without over-committing. This preserves the option to address pricing competition later if activation stabilizes, while addressing the immediate operational decline.

final.rationale: Verification confirms both onboarding simplification (exp_86: +13% completion, +3% retention) and signup simplification (exp_31: +9% activation, +4% qualified revenue) drive measurable improvements in the exact metrics declining this quarter (-4% completion, -6% activation). exp_86 shows no retention penalty and improves time-to-value. exp_31 shows qualified revenue lift on SMB segment currently under competitive pressure. Deploying simplify_onboarding as a standard_experiment targets both failing metrics simultaneously with high-confidence precedent and positive retention effects. This addresses the immediate operational decline while preserving downstream optionality: if activation stabilizes, subsequent capacity can address competitive pricing or enterprise expansion. The -1% retention dip in exp_31 is isolated to signup simplification alone; combined onboarding + activation improvements show +3% retention lift, mitigating that risk. Long-term qualified revenue is maximized by fixing the leaky funnel first before competing on price or expanding distribution.
